properties.description:
Seven tests across two crates, and the SPLIT between them is itself the finding.

**Core (4), over `DesignGraph`:** a report lands as a dated observation carrying `fact_type: manual_work`; the same work reported twice is ONE record (the id derives from `what`, so a count cannot inflate with re-tellings); an unknown `diagnosis` is REFUSED; and every report reads back through `manual_work_report` with its diagnosis and named tool intact.

**MCP (3), over the real `ReflowService`:** a report naming a tool the surface does not serve is refused; one naming `search_design` is kept; one naming NO tool is kept, because `tool_missing` names nothing by design and must not require one.

⭐ WHY THE SPLIT. "Does reflow2 serve a tool by this name?" was first written as a CORE test and failed there — the core does not know what the surface serves. Answering it there would have meant a second copy of the tool list maintained by hand, which is the defect class this project fixed three times on 2026-08-26. At the tool, `tool_router.has_route()` asks the LIVE ROUTER, so nothing is maintained and nothing can drift. Both files carry a note saying why the test lives where it does.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHECK, and it is the requirement's own standing objection: that a session will actually NOTICE it did something by hand. The mechanism depends on the agent having seen the tool it went without, which is the same blind spot it exists to measure. No test can reach that, and an empty `manual_work_report` is therefore never evidence that nothing was hand-rolled.
properties.findings:
7 passed / 0 failed (core 4, MCP 3). ⭐ WRITTEN BEFORE THE BUILD AND OBSERVED FAILING: the first run could not even compile, because `report_manual_work` and `manual_work_report` did not exist. One of the five original core tests then failed for a REASON RATHER THAN A BUG — the phantom-tool check cannot live in the core, which does not know what the surface serves — and moving it to the MCP crate is how the layering got decided rather than assumed.

Full workspace suite after: 1824 passed / 0 failed across 161 binaries, and the arithmetic reconciles exactly — 1817 before, plus 7 new tests, across 159 + 2 binaries. `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` clean on both crates; `skill_lint` all pass; `toolsnap` 163 match with the two new tools added.

📌 A METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING. Running `-p reflow2-core` plus `-p reflow2-mcp` separately is NOT equivalent to `--workspace`: it came to 1778 across 161 binaries, 46 tests short, because `reflow2-mcp` depends on core with `features = ["rocksdb"]` and a workspace build unifies that onto core while a solo run does not. Two binaries carried the whole difference (`reflow2_core` unittests 239 -> 201, `search` 9 -> 1). AGENTS.md documents the feature-unification fact; that it makes the split run a WEAKER check is the part that was not obvious and was nearly reported as equivalent.
properties.name: A by-hand report is dated, deduplicated, refuses a bad diagnosis or a phantom tool, and reads back
